{"self_assessment": "Impact: Our table built a fish that read clearly, with about 121 of 124 standing dominoes connected to the start. My contribution was quality assurance, not construction. I placed no dominoes myself. I inspected the tail and crossing area five times between 1:15 and 3:00, including the doubled-up stretch just before the crossing. Those checks helped confirm the joints were sound before we committed to hands-off.

Execution: I focused on the highest-risk part of the build, where the top and bottom lines cross near the tail. I looked closely at it repeatedly and reported what I saw to the table. I then held back from touching a structure that was already working, which avoided adding bump risk late on.

Collaboration: I kept communication clear and low-friction. I acknowledged the plan, stayed out of Hana's and Sofia's way while they laid the tail, and said when I would leave the top line alone. I supported the shared decision to go hands-off so nobody knocked anything over before the push. I also gave my teammates credit as the work came together.

Leadership: I led by restraint and by encouraging the team. I backed the decision to stop touching the table, helped keep the group calm and aligned in the final minutes, and kept the mood positive up to the push. Sofia's sketch and her and Hana's and Omar's building did most of the physical work. My part was smaller, but my inspections and support helped the team finish confident in the result.", "my_share_percent": 8}
